rows.description: A new intern or ragging-era junior does what a senior demands to avoid punishment or gain favour. Responsibility feels moved to the person giving the order, which is exactly how harm gets done.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Following a boss into a grey area [Actor]
rows.description: An employee is asked to backdate a form or smooth a report and complies, telling themselves it is not their decision. Diffused responsibility lets ordinary people do things they would never choose alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A colleague sees a peer quietly doing something dubious on instruction. Asking a plain question, is this okay, gives the person space to pause without being accused.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: An adult declines an improper instruction calmly, asks for it in writing, and uses proper channels. Wisdom is knowing that following orders never removes personal responsibility.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: Children playing a group game follow the confident child's plan even when a quieter child has a better idea. Nobody checks, because arguing seems to risk the fun and the friendship.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A group of teens planning an event rushes to agree with the loudest member. Nobody wants to spoil the mood, so doubts stay unspoken and a poor plan goes ahead.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A college project team dismisses a member's concern because the group feels united and confident. Cohesion feels good, so contrary evidence is treated as disloyalty.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A student keeps a reservation to themselves because everyone else looks certain. They assume the others must know better, not realising several others are silent for the same reason.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A team member suggests everyone note their concerns privately before the meeting. Collecting views before the group's mood forms keeps quiet voices from being drowned out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A team nods through a plan while each person privately has worries. Later, hallway chats reveal almost everyone had doubts, and the unity was an illusion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
